Advance Tax Due Dates, Schedule & Interest Penalties under Section 234B & 234C: 2026 Guide
Master the advance tax installment schedule, 15%-45%-75%-100% deadlines, computation rules, and how to avoid Section 234B & 234C interest penalties.

Under the Indian Income Tax Act, 1961, tax compliance follows the principle of **"Pay as You Earn"**. If your estimated net tax liability for a financial year (after accounting for TDS and TCS credits) is **₹10,000 or more**, paying tax at the time of filing your annual ITR is not sufficient. You are legally required to deposit advance tax across designated quarterly installments.

Failing to pay advance tax or deferring payments results in mandatory, compounding interest penalties under **Section 234B** (1% per month for shortfall) and **Section 234C** (1% per month for deferment).

Here is the complete operational guide to advance tax installments, calculation formulas, and penalty avoidance.

Do not risk manual estimation errors. Use our **[Free Advance Tax Calculator](/advance-tax-calculator)** to determine your exact quarterly payable amounts after TDS deductions and Section 87A rebates.

## Advance Tax Installment Schedule (Individual, Corporate & LLPs)

For all corporate assesses and non-corporate taxpayers (salaried individuals with side business/capital gains, professionals, partnerships, and LLPs):

| Installment Due Date | Statutory Cumulative Percentage Payable | How to Compute |
|---|---|---|
| **On or before June 15th** | **15%** of estimated net tax liability | Estimated annual tax × 15% - TDS/TCS |
| **On or before September 15th** | **45%** of estimated net tax liability | Estimated annual tax × 45% - Tax already paid |
| **On or before December 15th** | **75%** of estimated net tax liability | Estimated annual tax × 75% - Tax already paid |
| **On or before March 15th** | **100%** of estimated net tax liability | Estimated annual tax × 100% - Tax already paid |

> **Special Relief for Section 44AD / 44ADA Presumptive Taxpayers:**  
> Freelancers and small businesses opting for presumptive taxation are exempt from the 4-quarter schedule. They can deposit **100% of their advance tax in a single installment on or before March 15th**.

---

## Senior Citizen Exemption under Section 207

Senior citizens resident in India enjoy a complete exemption from advance tax obligations if:
1. They are aged **60 years or above** at any time during the financial year.
2. They do **not** have any income chargeable under the head "Profits and Gains of Business or Profession" (PGBP).

Senior citizens whose income comprises exclusively pension, interest on fixed deposits, rental income, and capital gains can pay their entire tax at the time of filing their ITR before July 31st without incurring Section 234B/234C interest penalties.

---

## Decoding Interest Penalties: Section 234C & Section 234B

### 1. Section 234C: Penalty for Deferment of Installments
Section 234C penalizes you if you pay less than the statutory percentage in any given quarter:
- **June 15th:** If tax paid is less than **12%** of final tax (statutory buffer of 3%), interest is charged @ **1% per month for 3 months** on the shortfall below 15%.
- **September 15th:** If tax paid is less than **36%** of final tax (statutory buffer of 9%), interest is charged @ **1% per month for 3 months** on the shortfall below 45%.
- **December 15th:** If tax paid is less than **75%**, interest is charged @ **1% per month for 3 months** on the shortfall below 75%.
- **March 15th:** If tax paid is less than **100%**, interest is charged @ **1% for 1 month** on the shortfall below 100%.

### 2. Section 234B: Penalty for Short-Payment (< 90%)
If by the end of the financial year (March 31st), your cumulative advance tax + TDS/TCS paid is **less than 90% of your assessed tax**, interest @ **1% per month (or part of a month)** is charged under Section 234B starting from April 1st of the Assessment Year until the date of actual payment.

---

## Advance Tax on Unexpected Capital Gains or Lottery Winnings

What happens if you sell a property, redeem mutual funds, or book stock market profits in February? How could you have paid advance tax for that in June or September?

The law provides a specific safeguard under the **proviso to Section 234C**:
- If a shortfall occurs due to sudden capital gains, speculative gains (lottery/games), or new business income, **no Section 234C penalty is levied** provided you pay the full remaining tax in the subsequent installment dates.
- If the capital gain occurred after March 15th, you must deposit the tax on or before **March 31st** to escape interest.

## How to Pay Advance Tax Online (Step-by-Step)

1. Visit the official e-Filing Income Tax portal (`eportal.incometax.gov.in`).
2. Navigate to **e-Pay Tax** under Quick Links.
3. Enter your **PAN / TAN** and confirm via mobile OTP.
4. Select **Income Tax** and click *Proceed*.
5. Choose **Assessment Year (AY 2026-27 for FY 2025-26)**.
6. Under Type of Payment, strictly select **Advance Tax (100)**.
7. Enter the tax breakdown under Tax, Surcharge, and Cess.
8. Complete payment via Net Banking, Debit Card, RTGS/NEFT, or UPI. Download the generated **Challan Form (CRN / BSR Code / Challan No.)** for your records.

### What if my salary already has TDS deducted by my employer?
If your employer deducts sufficient TDS covering your full salary income, your net advance tax liability is zero. However, if you have substantial interest from bank FDs, dividend income, or rental income that you did not disclose to your employer, you must personally calculate and pay advance tax on those supplementary incomes if the net tax exceeds ₹10,000.

### Can I pay advance tax after March 15th?
Any tax paid on or before **March 31st** of the financial year is legally treated as advance tax under Section 211(1). However, delaying past March 15th will attract 1% interest for 1 month under Section 234C.

How to Calculate GST Late Fees in 2026: A Complete Guide
Learn how to accurately calculate GST late fees for GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, and GSTR-9. Understand maximum caps, nil return waivers, and penalty rules.

Navigating the Indian Goods and Services Tax (GST) landscape requires meticulous attention to deadlines. Missing a due date for filing your GST returns—whether it's GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, or the annual GSTR-9—inevitably leads to the accrual of late fees. In the early days of GST, the penalty structures were largely uniform, but moving into 2026, the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) has refined the rules, introducing tiered maximum caps based on a taxpayer's Annual Aggregate Turnover (AATO).

Understanding exactly how these late fees are calculated, what the maximum caps are, and how interest compounds on outstanding tax liabilities is absolutely critical for any business owner, freelancer, or accountant. While you can manually calculate these figures using complex formulas, the most efficient method is to rely on automated tools like our [Late Fee Calculator](/late-fee-calculator). 

In this comprehensive guide, we will break down the exact mathematics behind GST late fees, the nuances of nil returns, and the strategies you can employ to minimize your financial exposure.

---

## The Mathematics of GST Late Fees

Under the CGST Act, late fees are automatically levied by the GSTN portal for every single day of delay from the original due date until the actual date of filing. The fee is charged under two heads: CGST (Central GST) and SGST (State GST).

### Standard Late Fee Rates

For standard monthly or quarterly returns (like GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B), the baseline per-day calculation is:
- **₹25 under CGST + ₹25 under SGST = ₹50 per day of delay.**

However, if you had absolutely no business activity during that period and are filing a **Nil Return**, the government provides a massive reduction:
- **₹10 under CGST + ₹10 under SGST = ₹20 per day of delay.**

*Example Calculation:* 
If your GSTR-3B was due on the 20th of August, and you file it on the 25th of August, the delay is 5 days.
- Standard Return: 5 days × ₹50 = ₹250 late fee.
- Nil Return: 5 days × ₹20 = ₹100 late fee.

It is critical to note that late fees must be paid entirely in cash through the electronic cash ledger. You absolutely **cannot** use your Input Tax Credit (ITC) balance to offset a late fee penalty.

## Maximum Late Fee Caps Based on Turnover

To prevent exorbitant penalties from destroying small businesses, the CBIC introduced a rationalized capping system. The maximum late fee you can be charged for GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B is capped based on your previous year's turnover.

### 1. Nil Returns (Zero Tax Liability)
If your return has zero tax liability for the month/quarter, the maximum late fee is strictly capped at **₹500** (₹250 CGST + ₹250 SGST).

### 2. Turnover up to ₹1.5 Crore
For micro-enterprises with an AATO up to ₹1.5 Crore, the maximum late fee is capped at **₹2,000** (₹1,000 CGST + ₹1,000 SGST).

### 3. Turnover between ₹1.5 Crore and ₹5 Crore
For small to medium enterprises in this bracket, the late fee is capped at **₹5,000** (₹2,500 CGST + ₹2,500 SGST).

### 4. Turnover Above ₹5 Crore
For large enterprises exceeding ₹5 Crore, there is a much higher cap. The maximum late fee can reach up to **₹10,000** (₹5,000 CGST + ₹5,000 SGST).

These caps apply per return. If you fail to file both GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B for six months, these caps will apply to *each* of those twelve pending returns, leading to a massive financial burden. You should regularly check our [GST Due Dates](/gst-due-dates) page to ensure you never miss a filing deadline.

---

## The Difference Between Late Fees and Interest

A common point of confusion is conflating late fees with interest. They are two distinct penalties that operate simultaneously.

- **Late Fee**: A penalty for failing to file the return document on time. It is calculated at ₹50 per day.
- **Interest**: A penalty for failing to pay the actual tax money to the government on time. 

If you file your GSTR-3B late, and you also had a net cash tax liability to pay, you will be hit with both. Interest is calculated at **18% per annum** on the net cash tax liability, computed from the day immediately following the due date until the date of actual payment. 

*Crucial Update for 2026*: Interest is only charged on the portion of tax paid in cash (the electronic cash ledger). It is not charged on the portion of tax offset using Input Tax Credit (ITC), provided you have not utilized the ITC fraudulently.

## How to Calculate GSTR-9 (Annual Return) Late Fees

The annual return, GSTR-9, carries a completely different, much steeper penalty structure compared to monthly returns. 

The baseline per-day delay charge is higher:
- **₹100 under CGST + ₹100 under SGST = ₹200 per day of delay.**

Furthermore, the maximum cap is calculated differently. Instead of a flat rupee amount, the maximum late fee is capped at **0.50% of your total turnover in the respective State/UT** (0.25% CGST + 0.25% SGST). 

For a company with a ₹10 Crore turnover in Maharashtra, 0.50% equates to ₹5,00,000. Therefore, delaying the GSTR-9 can result in catastrophic financial penalties that vastly outweigh the penalties of monthly returns. 

If you are dealing with large invoices, always double-check the applicable rates using an [HSN Code Finder](/hsn-code-lookup) and our [GST Calculator](/gst-calculator) before finalization. Furthermore, ensure the vendors you are dealing with are active using our [GSTIN Validator](/gstin-validator) to prevent ITC mismatches which delay your annual reconciliation.

---

## Best Practices to Avoid Late Fees

1. **Leverage the QRMP Scheme**: If your turnover is under ₹5 Crore, opt into the Quarterly Return Filing and Monthly Payment of Taxes (QRMP) scheme. This reduces your GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B filing frequency from 24 times a year to just 8, massively reducing the chances of missing a deadline.
2. **File Nil Returns Promptly**: Even if you have zero sales and zero purchases for a month, you must file a Nil Return. The GST portal allows you to file a Nil GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B via SMS in seconds. Neglecting to do so will result in a ₹20/day penalty.
3. **Reconcile Continuously**: Do not wait until the 18th of the month to begin reconciling your purchase data with GSTR-2B. Use modern accounting software to reconcile weekly.
4. **Automate Reminders**: Bookmark our [Due Dates](/gst-due-dates) page and set up calendar alerts 3 days prior to the 11th (GSTR-1) and 20th (GSTR-3B) of every month.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Q1: Can GST late fees be waived?**
A: Under normal circumstances, no. Late fees are hard-coded into the GSTN portal. However, the government occasionally announces "Amnesty Schemes" (usually during extreme economic hardship or pandemics) where late fees for specific past periods are heavily reduced or capped.

**Q2: I have sufficient ITC in my ledger. Can I use it to pay my late fee?**
A: No. Section 49 of the CGST Act strictly mandates that late fees, interest, and penalties can only be paid via cash deposited into the Electronic Cash Ledger. 

**Q3: If I file GSTR-1 late, do I pay the late fee immediately?**
A: No, the GST portal automatically calculates the late fee for a delayed GSTR-1 and adds it to the liability of your *subsequent* GSTR-3B return. You will be forced to pay it before the system allows you to file the next 3B.

**Q4: Is there a late fee for delaying GSTR-2A or 2B?**
A: GSTR-2A and 2B are auto-populated, read-only statements based on your suppliers' filings. Therefore, you do not "file" them, and there are no late fees associated with them.

4-Digit vs 6-Digit HSN Codes: What is the Rule for 2026?
Understand the latest CBIC rules regarding 4-digit, 6-digit, and 8-digit HSN codes on GST invoices based on your turnover limit in India.

Entering the correct Harmonized System of Nomenclature (HSN) code on a tax invoice is an absolutely critical legal requirement under the Indian Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime. However, the exact level of detail required—specifically the number of digits—has been a constant source of confusion for many business owners, chartered accountants, and tax professionals.

As we move deeper into 2026, the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) continues to refine its stance on data granularity to curb tax evasion and ensure precise policy formulation. If your business generates B2B (Business-to-Business) or B2C (Business-to-Consumer) invoices, you must perfectly understand the rules regarding 4-digit versus 6-digit HSN codes. Failing to comply can lead to rejected e-invoices, mismatched GSTR-1 returns, and substantial financial penalties.

You can instantly search for the exact format required for your specific products using our incredibly fast, entirely free [HSN Code Lookup](/hsn-code-lookup) tool, which tracks over 13,000 active codes.

---

## What is an HSN Code and Why Does it Matter?

Before diving into the complex turnover limits, it is important to understand what these codes actually represent. Developed by the World Customs Organization (WCO), the Harmonized System of Nomenclature is an internationally accepted method of classifying goods. 

Under the Indian GST system, an HSN code serves multiple vital functions:
1. **Determining the GST Slab**: The code links directly to a specific GST rate (0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, or 28%). Without the code, determining the correct tax is impossible. Use our [GST Calculator](/gst-calculator) once you find your code.
2. **Data Analytics**: It allows the government to track exactly what types of goods are moving across state borders.
3. **E-Way Bills and E-Invoicing**: Modern GST compliance requires real-time data validation. The National Informatics Centre (NIC) portal will outright reject an e-invoice if the HSN code is missing or structurally invalid.

## The Definitive ₹5 Crore Turnover Rule

The CBIC has structured the HSN reporting requirements based entirely on a business's Aggregate Annual Turnover (AATO) in the preceding financial year. This tiered approach was designed to reduce the compliance burden on smaller Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) while demanding more granular data from larger corporations.

### 1. Businesses with Turnover up to ₹5 Crore

If your AATO in the previous financial year was ₹5 Crore or less, the government offers a slightly relaxed reporting environment.

- **B2B Invoices (Business to Business)**: You **MUST** mention a minimum of a **4-digit HSN Code**. This applies to all tax invoices raised against another registered taxpayer. 
- **B2C Invoices (Business to Consumer)**: Mentioning the HSN code on B2C invoices is technically **Optional**. However, it is highly recommended as a best practice, especially if you plan to scale your business or if your accounting software handles it automatically.

### 2. Businesses with Turnover Above ₹5 Crore

If your business has scaled past the ₹5 Crore threshold, you fall into the higher compliance bracket. The government requires precise, item-level classification.

- **All Invoices (Both B2B and B2C)**: You **MUST** mention a minimum of a **6-digit HSN Code**. There are absolutely no exceptions here. Every invoice, whether you are selling a bulk shipment of steel to a manufacturer or a single laptop to an unregistered end-consumer, must feature a 6-digit code.

---

## 8-Digit HSN Codes: When Are They Required?

57th GST Council Meeting Recap: Key Decisions, Rate Rationalizations & Compliance Changes

Comprehensive recap of the 57th GST Council meeting decisions. Learn about Section 128A amnesty deadlines, GSTAT operationalization, insurance premium rate rationalizations, and biometric Aadhaar rollouts.

The GST Council, chaired by Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman alongside state finance ministers, serves as India's apex constitutional decision-making body on indirect taxes. The **57th GST Council meeting** addressed critical ongoing litigation backlogs, operationalized dispute resolution bodies, rationalized tariffs on essential services, and rolled out advanced anti-evasion compliance architecture.

For business owners, corporate tax directors, and chartered accountants, staying updated with these council resolutions is vital for timely tax planning.

Here is the complete analytical recap of the key decisions, procedural simplifications, and statutory reforms enacted by the 57th GST Council.

---

## Check Your Amnesty & Rate Eligibility

- Check whether your pending demand notices for FY 2017-18 to 2019-20 qualify for 100% waiver of interest and penalties under Section 128A on our **[GST Amnesty Tracker](/gst-amnesty-tracker)**.
- Search the updated tariff schedules and exemptions on our **[GST Rate & SAC Finder](/gst-rate-finder)**.

---

## 1. Operational Guidelines for Section 128A Amnesty Scheme

One of the most consequential taxpayer-friendly measures deliberated was the procedural framework for **Section 128A of the CGST Act**, introduced to relieve honest businesses from crushing interest and penalty liabilities:

- **Coverage:** Applicable to Show Cause Notices and demand orders issued under **Section 73 (non-fraudulent cases)** for the first three years of GST rollout: **FY 2017-18, FY 2018-19, and FY 2019-20**.
- **The Relief:** If the taxpayer deposits **100% of the basic disputed tax liability** on or before the notified statutory cutoff date, **100% of interest under Section 50 and 100% of penalties are completely waived**.
- **No Refund of Already Paid Penalties:** The Council clarified that if a taxpayer had already discharged the penalty or interest prior to the scheme notification, no refund of such payments will be granted.
- **Exclusions:** Does not apply to demand orders issued under Section 74 (fraud, willful misstatement, suppression of facts) or demands relating to erroneous refunds.

---

## 2. GSTAT Benches & Pre-Deposit Rationalization

With the long-awaited operationalization of the **Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT)**:
- **Tribunal Infrastructure:** Benches are now active across 31 State and Principal locations, allowing taxpayers to file second appeals instead of moving High Courts via Article 226 writ petitions.
- **Pre-Deposit Relief:** The pre-deposit required for filing an appeal before the Appellate Authority under Section 107 remains at 10% (capped at ₹20 Crores). The pre-deposit for filing before GSTAT under Section 112 was confirmed at **20% of the disputed tax** (with rationalized lower caps for MSMEs).
- **Anti-Profiteering Transition:** The sunset date for anti-profiteering matters was solidified, with remaining price monitoring cases transferred directly to the Competition Commission of India (CCI) and designated High Court appellate divisions.

---

## 3. Rate Rationalization & Health Insurance Exemptions

The Council deliberated extensively on Group of Ministers (GoM) recommendations regarding the rationalization of rate slabs and humanitarian exemptions:

| Commodity / Service | Previous GST Rate | Recommended / Revised Rate | Statutory Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Term Life & Senior Citizen Health Insurance** | 18% | **0% (EXEMPT)** / Concessional | Major cost relief for retail policyholders and pensioners |
| **Individual Health Insurance (Coverage up to ₹5L)** | 18% | **Reduced / Exempt** | Aimed at universal health coverage expansion |
| **Agricultural Bio-Pesticides & Micronutrients** | 12% / 18% | **5%** | Encouraging sustainable organic farming practices |
| **Selected Renewable Energy Components** | 12% | **5%** | Fostering domestic solar equipment manufacturing |
| **Luxury & Sin Goods Compensation Cess Slabs** | 28% + Cess | **Rationalized Post-Cess Transition** | Preparing for post-March 2026 debt repayment phase |

---

## 4. Nationwide Biometric-Based Aadhaar Authentication

To combat the menace of fake invoice syndicates, bogus shell firms, and circular trading, the Council approved the nationwide rollout of **Biometric-Based Aadhaar Authentication**:

- **Risk-Based Trigger:** Taxpayers applying for new GST registration who are identified as "high-risk" by DGARM algorithms must complete biometric verification.
- **Physical Verification Centers:** Applicants are scheduled for in-person biometric scanning (fingerprint and iris scan) along with physical verification of the principal place of business before GSTIN approval.
- **Impact on Honest Businesses:** Genuine applicants with clean PAN histories and verified Aadhaar-linked OTPs continue to receive automated approvals within 3 to 7 working days.

---

## 5. Invoice Management System (IMS) Integration

The Council reviewed the nationwide implementation of the **Invoice Management System (IMS)**:
- A new interactive dashboard introduced on the GST portal allowing recipient taxpayers to actively **Accept, Reject, or Keep Pending** each inward invoice uploaded by suppliers in GSTR-1.
- Accepted invoices flow directly into **Form GSTR-2B**, locking in eligible Input Tax Credit and eliminating year-end reconciliation disputes.

---

## Summary of Key Takeaways for Taxpayers

1. **Review Section 73 Notices Immediately:** Run an audit of all pending demands from FY 2017-18 to 2019-20 to take advantage of the Section 128A interest and penalty waiver before deadlines elapse.
2. **Implement IMS Review Protocols:** Direct your accounts payable teams to reconcile and accept supplier invoices on the IMS dashboard weekly.
3. **Verify Vendor GSTINs:** With enhanced biometric screening, eliminate unverified or suspended vendors from your procurement cycle to protect your Input Tax Credit.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### Does the Section 128A waiver apply to cases where an appeal is pending?
Yes. If an appeal is pending before the First Appellate Authority or GSTAT, you can still apply for the Section 128A waiver by withdrawing the appeal, paying the full basic tax amount, and submitting proof to the Proper Officer.

### When will the final insurance GST rate reductions take legal effect?
GST Council recommendations take legal effect only after the Central Government and respective State Governments issue formal statutory rate notifications. Always refer to official CBIC notifications for exact enforcement dates.

ASMT-10 vs DRC-01 GST Notice: Key Differences, Timelines & Legal Reply Formats
Confused between ASMT-10 scrutiny notice and DRC-01 Show Cause Notice? Learn the procedural differences, statutory time limits, Form ASMT-11 reply formats, and defense tactics.

Receiving a communication from the GST department can be intimidating, but mistaking a preliminary scrutiny notice for a formal demand order can lead to costly mistakes. The two most common notices received by GST taxpayers are **Form GST ASMT-10** and **Form GST DRC-01**.

While ASMT-10 is an advisory discrepancy notice issued during return scrutiny under **Section 61**, DRC-01 is a formal Show Cause Notice (SCN) issued under **Section 73 or 74** initiating quasi-judicial demand proceedings.

In this guide, we break down the statutory difference between ASMT-10 and DRC-01, the procedural progression from one to the other, and provide exact reply strategies and templates.

---

## Generate a Legal Reply to Your Notice

Need to draft a formal, legally grounded response to an ASMT-10 or DRC-01 notice right now? Use our **[AI GST Notice Reply Generator](/gst-notice-reply-generator)** to instantly insert relevant CBIC circulars, reconciliations, and statutory hearing prayers.

---

## Direct Comparison: ASMT-10 vs DRC-01

| Feature | Form GST ASMT-10 | Form GST DRC-01 |
|---|---|---|
| **Statutory Section** | Section 61 read with Rule 99 | Section 73 (non-fraud) or Section 74 (fraud) read with Rule 142 |
| **Nature of Document** | Scrutiny of Returns notice pointing out discrepancies | Formal Show Cause Notice (SCN) demanding tax, interest, & penalty |
| **Binding Tax Demand?** | No. Only highlights differences (GSTR-3B vs 1 or 2B) | Yes. Quantifies exact tax, interest under Sec 50, and penalties |
| **Statutory Reply Form** | **Form GST ASMT-11** via the GST Portal | **Form GST DRC-06** via the GST Portal |
| **Standard Reply Time** | Maximum **30 days** (or extended time granted by proper officer) | Strictly **30 days** from date of service |
| **Departmental Follow-Up** | If satisfied: **ASMT-12** (Dropped). If not: Initiates Audit/DRC-01A/DRC-01 | If satisfied: **DRC-05** (Dropped). If not: Demand Order in **DRC-07** |
| **Recovery Actions?** | No bank attachment or recovery possible | Failure to reply leads to DRC-07 followed by Section 79 bank attachment |

---

## How an ASMT-10 Notice Progresses

Understanding the departmental workflow helps you nip disputes in the bud before they become irreversible liabilities:

```
[Return Scrutiny (Section 61)]
          │
          ▼
   [Form ASMT-10 Issued]
          │
          ▼
  [Taxpayer Files ASMT-11 Reply within 30 Days]
          │
  ┌───────┴───────────────────────────────┐
  ▼                                       ▼
[Officer Satisfied]             [Discrepancies Unresolved]
  │                                       │
  ▼                                       ▼
[ASMT-12 Issued: Closed]         [Pre-Notice Intimation in DRC-01A]
                                          │
                                          ▼
                                 [Formal SCN in DRC-01]
                                          │
                                          ▼
                                 [Final Demand in DRC-07]
```

---

## What Triggers an ASMT-10 Notice?

The GST Directorate General of Analytics and Risk Management (DGARM) flags accounts automatically based on data algorithms:
1. **Outward Supply Mismatch:** GSTR-1 outward turnover is greater than GSTR-3B reported turnover.
2. **Inward ITC Mismatch:** Input Tax Credit claimed in Table 4(A)(5) of GSTR-3B exceeds eligible ITC available in GSTR-2B.
3. **E-Way Bill vs GSTR-1:** Significant variance between generated E-Way bills and outward supplies declared in returns.
4. **ITC from Cancelled Vendors:** Claiming ITC against suppliers whose GST registration was cancelled retrospectively.
5. **RCM Liability Shortfall:** Higher purchases from unregistered suppliers or GTA freight without corresponding Reverse Charge liability paid in Table 3.1(d).

---

## Step-by-Step Blueprint: Replying to ASMT-10 in Form ASMT-11

### Step 1: Download the Annexure from the Portal
Log into `gst.gov.in` → Services → User Services → View Additional Notices and Orders. Locate the ASMT-10 order and download the detailed Excel sheet or PDF containing the discrepancy table.

### Step 2: Reconcile with Invoice Level Data
Do not reply with generic denials. Prepare a mathematical reconciliation table comparing:
- Invoice numbers and dates
- Supplier GSTINs and filing dates
- Reasons for timing differences (e.g., ITC claimed in following month, credit notes accounted later).

### Step 3: Draft Your ASMT-11 Submission
Structure your reply under 4 standard legal heads:
- **Reference:** Cite the notice reference number and date.
- **Point-by-Point Clarification:** Address each discrepancy serial number specifically.
- **Statutory & Judicial Precedents:** Refer to relevant CBIC circulars (e.g., Circular No. 183/15/2022-GST for FY 2017-18 / 2018-19 ITC mismatches).
- **Prayer:** Explicitly request the Proper Officer to accept the explanation and issue an acceptance order in **Form GST ASMT-12**.

---

## Reply Strategy When Moving to DRC-01

If your ASMT-11 was rejected or if the department skipped ASMT-10 and issued DRC-01 directly:
- File your reply in **Form DRC-06** within 30 days.
- Under **Section 75(4) of the CGST Act**, an opportunity of personal hearing is **mandatory** before any adverse decision or order is passed. Always include the statutory hearing prayer:  
  *"Without prejudice to the above submissions, the taxpayer requests a personal hearing before any adverse demand order is finalized."*
- Failure by the officer to grant a personal hearing renders the subsequent DRC-07 order null and void in High Court writ jurisdiction for violation of natural justice.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### What if I agree with the discrepancy in ASMT-10?
If you agree that tax was genuinely short-paid, deposit the tax along with interest under Section 50 using **Form GST DRC-03** (selecting "Voluntary" or "Scrutiny"). In your ASMT-11 reply, attach the DRC-03 payment receipt. The officer will close proceedings via ASMT-12 without imposing penal charges.

### Can an officer issue DRC-01 without issuing ASMT-10?
Yes. Multiple High Courts (including Madras and Gujarat High Courts) have held that Section 61 (ASMT-10) is not a mandatory prerequisite for issuing a demand under Section 73 or 74. If the department has independent audit findings or intelligence, they can directly issue DRC-01A and DRC-01.

Receiving a communication from the GST department can be intimidating, but mistaking a preliminary scrutiny notice for a formal demand order can lead to costly mistakes. The two most common notices received by GST taxpayers are Form GST ASMT-10 and Form GST DRC-01.

While ASMT-10 is an advisory discrepancy notice issued during return scrutiny under Section 61, DRC-01 is a formal Show Cause Notice (SCN) issued under Section 73 or 74 initiating quasi-judicial demand proceedings.

In this guide, we break down the statutory difference between ASMT-10 and DRC-01, the procedural progression from one to the other, and provide exact reply strategies and templates.

What Triggers an ASMT-10 Notice?

The GST Directorate General of Analytics and Risk Management (DGARM) flags accounts automatically based on data algorithms:

  1. Outward Supply Mismatch: GSTR-1 outward turnover is greater than GSTR-3B reported turnover.
  2. Inward ITC Mismatch: Input Tax Credit claimed in Table 4(A)(5) of GSTR-3B exceeds eligible ITC available in GSTR-2B.
  3. E-Way Bill vs GSTR-1: Significant variance between generated E-Way bills and outward supplies declared in returns.
  4. ITC from Cancelled Vendors: Claiming ITC against suppliers whose GST registration was cancelled retrospectively.
  5. RCM Liability Shortfall: Higher purchases from unregistered suppliers or GTA freight without corresponding Reverse Charge liability paid in Table 3.1(d).

Step-by-Step Blueprint: Replying to ASMT-10 in Form ASMT-11

Step 1: Download the Annexure from the Portal

Log into gst.gov.in → Services → User Services → View Additional Notices and Orders. Locate the ASMT-10 order and download the detailed Excel sheet or PDF containing the discrepancy table.

Step 2: Reconcile with Invoice Level Data

Do not reply with generic denials. Prepare a mathematical reconciliation table comparing:

  • Invoice numbers and dates
  • Supplier GSTINs and filing dates
  • Reasons for timing differences (e.g., ITC claimed in following month, credit notes accounted later).

Step 3: Draft Your ASMT-11 Submission

Structure your reply under 4 standard legal heads:

  • Reference: Cite the notice reference number and date.
  • Point-by-Point Clarification: Address each discrepancy serial number specifically.
  • Statutory & Judicial Precedents: Refer to relevant CBIC circulars (e.g., Circular No. 183/15/2022-GST for FY 2017-18 / 2018-19 ITC mismatches).
  • Prayer: Explicitly request the Proper Officer to accept the explanation and issue an acceptance order in Form GST ASMT-12.

Reply Strategy When Moving to DRC-01

If your ASMT-11 was rejected or if the department skipped ASMT-10 and issued DRC-01 directly:

  • File your reply in Form DRC-06 within 30 days.
  • Under Section 75(4) of the CGST Act, an opportunity of personal hearing is mandatory before any adverse decision or order is passed. Always include the statutory hearing prayer:
    “Without prejudice to the above submissions, the taxpayer requests a personal hearing before any adverse demand order is finalized.”
  • Failure by the officer to grant a personal hearing renders the subsequent DRC-07 order null and void in High Court writ jurisdiction for violation of natural justice.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

What if I agree with the discrepancy in ASMT-10?

If you agree that tax was genuinely short-paid, deposit the tax along with interest under Section 50 using Form GST DRC-03 (selecting “Voluntary” or “Scrutiny”). In your ASMT-11 reply, attach the DRC-03 payment receipt. The officer will close proceedings via ASMT-12 without imposing penal charges.

Can an officer issue DRC-01 without issuing ASMT-10?

Yes. Multiple High Courts (including Madras and Gujarat High Courts) have held that Section 61 (ASMT-10) is not a mandatory prerequisite for issuing a demand under Section 73 or 74. If the department has independent audit findings or intelligence, they can directly issue DRC-01A and DRC-01.

The GST Composition Scheme was introduced to significantly reduce the compliance burden for small businesses. Instead of filing monthly GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B returns, composition taxpayers file a simple quarterly statement known as **Form CMP-08**.
Quick Answer: Form CMP-08 is due on the 18th of the month following the end of each quarter (July 18, October 18, January 18, and April 18). Late payment attracts statutory interest at 18% per annum u/s 50, calculated on net cash liability.

How to Calculate GST on Freight and Transportation Services
A comprehensive guide to understanding GST rates on freight, the Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM), and Input Tax Credit rules for transportation in 2026.

The logistics and transportation sector is the circulatory system of the Indian economy. However, calculating the Goods and Services Tax (GST) on freight charges remains one of the most complex aspects of GST compliance. Unlike a simple sale of a physical product, transportation involves multiple variables: the mode of transport (road, rail, air, sea), the status of the transporter (GTA vs. courier agency), and the specific contract terms (FOB vs. CIF).

Furthermore, the introduction of the Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM) heavily impacts who is legally responsible for paying the tax to the government—the transporter or the business receiving the service. As supply chains modernize in 2026, understanding these rules is critical to avoid massive compliance penalties and to ensure you are maximizing your Input Tax Credit (ITC).

This definitive guide breaks down how to correctly calculate GST on freight, when RCM applies, and how to verify the correct SAC classifications using tools like our [HSN Code Lookup](/hsn-code-lookup).

---

## 1. What is a Goods Transport Agency (GTA)?

Under the GST framework, the rules differ drastically depending on whether the transporter is classified as a Goods Transport Agency (GTA) or simply an individual truck owner. 

A **GTA** is legally defined as any person who provides service in relation to the transport of goods by road and *issues a consignment note*. The issuance of this consignment note is the defining factor. If a local truck owner simply moves your goods without issuing a formal consignment note, they are exempt from GST entirely.

If you are dealing with a registered GTA, you must ensure their GSTIN is valid using our instant [GSTIN Validator](/gstin-validator) before processing their invoice.

## 2. Forward Charge vs. Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM)

When you hire a GTA, the tax can be paid in one of two ways. In 2026, the CBIC continues to offer GTAs the option to choose their tax structure at the beginning of the financial year.

### The Forward Charge Option
Under the Forward Charge Mechanism (FCM), the GTA charges GST directly on the invoice, collects the tax from you, and pays it to the government. 
The GTA has two distinct rate options under FCM:
- **5% GST (No ITC)**: The GTA charges 5% but is legally barred from claiming Input Tax Credit on their own operational expenses (like truck purchases or maintenance).
- **12% GST (With ITC)**: The GTA charges 12% and is allowed to claim full ITC on their operational expenses.

### The Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM)
Under RCM, the GTA does *not* charge GST on the invoice. Instead, you (the business receiving the service) are legally required to calculate the GST at **5%**, pay it directly to the government out of your electronic cash ledger, and then claim it back as ITC. 

This mechanism is mandatory if the GTA has not opted for Forward Charge and you are a registered business entity, factory, society, or partnership firm. Always use an accurate [GST Calculator](/gst-calculator) to compute your exact RCM liability before filing your GSTR-3B.

---

## 3. GST Rates Based on Mode of Transport

If you are not using road transport via a GTA, the GST rates vary significantly based on the mode of transport.

### Railway Transport
Transporting goods by rail generally attracts a GST rate of **5%**. This is heavily subsidized to encourage bulk movement via the rail network. The railways will charge this under Forward Charge, and you can claim ITC subject to normal conditions.

### Air Freight (Domestic vs. International)
- **Domestic Air Freight**: Goods transported by air within India attract an **18% GST** rate.
- **International Air Freight**: The government frequently updates the rules regarding export freight. Historically, export air freight was exempt, but you must always verify the current 2026 notification status or consult an expert, as exemptions have sunset dates.

### Ocean/Sea Freight
- **Coastal Shipping (Domestic)**: Transporting goods by vessel along the Indian coast attracts a **5% GST** rate.
- **Import Ocean Freight**: If you import goods on a CIF (Cost, Insurance, and Freight) basis, the foreign supplier pays the shipping line. However, under a highly litigated GST provision, the Indian importer was historically required to pay 5% IGST on reverse charge on the ocean freight. *Note: Following Supreme Court rulings, the taxation of CIF import freight has evolved, and you should not pay IGST twice if it's already included in the customs assessable value.*

### Courier Agencies
Unlike GTAs, courier services operate entirely under the Forward Charge Mechanism. If you use a reputed courier company (e.g., BlueDart, Delhivery) to send parcels, they will charge you a flat **18% GST**. 

---

## 4. Calculating GST on "Composite Supply" Freight

One of the biggest mistakes businesses make is calculating freight GST incorrectly when it is bundled with the sale of goods.

If you are a manufacturer selling machinery for ₹1,00,000 (which attracts 18% GST) and you charge the customer an additional ₹5,000 for delivery on the same invoice, how do you tax the ₹5,000?

Under Section 8 of the CGST Act, this is classified as a **Composite Supply**. The principal supply is the machinery. The freight is naturally bundled with it. 
Therefore, the freight charge will inherit the GST rate of the principal supply. 
- You do *not* charge 5% on the freight. 
- You must charge **18%** on the entire ₹1,05,000.

Failing to apply the composite supply rule will lead to severe underpayment of taxes and subsequent departmental notices. If you are selling a bundle of goods with varying rates, always use our [GST Calculator](/gst-calculator) to determine the weighted average or principal rate.

## 5. E-Way Bill Requirements for Freight

Regardless of whether the tax is paid under Forward Charge or RCM, the physical movement of goods requires documentation. 

If the consignment value exceeds ₹50,000, an **E-Way Bill** is strictly mandatory. The responsibility to generate the E-Way Bill primarily lies with the supplier. However, if the supplier fails to do so, the transporter (GTA) is required to generate it before moving the vehicle.

The E-Way Bill must accurately reflect the HSN code of the goods being transported. Ensure your dispatch team uses our [HSN Code Lookup](/hsn-code-lookup) to prevent vehicle detentions at state borders. Any mismatch between the invoice and the E-Way Bill can result in a penalty equivalent to 200% of the tax amount.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Q1: Can I claim Input Tax Credit (ITC) if I pay 5% GST on GTA services under RCM?**
A: Yes. As the recipient of the service paying tax under RCM, you are fully eligible to claim the 5% as ITC in the same month, provided the transportation relates to the furtherance of your business.

**Q2: What is the SAC Code for Goods Transport Agency services?**
A: The Services Accounting Code (SAC) for goods transport by road by a GTA is **9965**. You can verify the exact structure in our comprehensive [HSN/SAC Code Finder](/hsn-code-lookup).

**Q3: Are there any exemptions for GTA services?**
A: Yes. Transporting specific goods like agricultural produce, milk, salt, food grain, organic manure, and defense/military equipment by a GTA is entirely exempt from GST.

**Q4: If I hire a local tempo for ₹1,000 and he doesn't issue a consignment note, do I pay RCM?**
A: No. Since no consignment note is issued, the transporter is not classified as a GTA. The service is exempt from GST, and no RCM liability arises.

By correctly classifying your logistics contracts and understanding the nuances of the Reverse Charge Mechanism, you can optimize your supply chain costs and eliminate the risk of late fees. Keep an eye on our [Due Dates Calendar](/gst-due-dates) to ensure your RCM liabilities are discharged on time.

One of the biggest mistakes businesses make is calculating freight GST incorrectly when it is bundled with the sale of goods.

If you are a manufacturer selling machinery for ₹1,00,000 (which attracts 18% GST) and you charge the customer an additional ₹5,000 for delivery on the same invoice, how do you tax the ₹5,000?

Under Section 8 of the CGST Act, this is classified as a Composite Supply. The principal supply is the machinery. The freight is naturally bundled with it. Therefore, the freight charge will inherit the GST rate of the principal supply.

  • You do not charge 5% on the freight.
  • You must charge 18% on the entire ₹1,05,000.

Failing to apply the composite supply rule will lead to severe underpayment of taxes and subsequent departmental notices. If you are selling a bundle of goods with varying rates, always use our GST Calculator to determine the weighted average or principal rate.

5. E-Way Bill Requirements for Freight

Regardless of whether the tax is paid under Forward Charge or RCM, the physical movement of goods requires documentation.

If the consignment value exceeds ₹50,000, an E-Way Bill is strictly mandatory. The responsibility to generate the E-Way Bill primarily lies with the supplier. However, if the supplier fails to do so, the transporter (GTA) is required to generate it before moving the vehicle.

The E-Way Bill must accurately reflect the HSN code of the goods being transported. Ensure your dispatch team uses our HSN Code Lookup to prevent vehicle detentions at state borders. Any mismatch between the invoice and the E-Way Bill can result in a penalty equivalent to 200% of the tax amount.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q1: Can I claim Input Tax Credit (ITC) if I pay 5% GST on GTA services under RCM? A: Yes. As the recipient of the service paying tax under RCM, you are fully eligible to claim the 5% as ITC in the same month, provided the transportation relates to the furtherance of your business.

Q2: What is the SAC Code for Goods Transport Agency services? A: The Services Accounting Code (SAC) for goods transport by road by a GTA is 9965. You can verify the exact structure in our comprehensive HSN/SAC Code Finder.

Q3: Are there any exemptions for GTA services? A: Yes. Transporting specific goods like agricultural produce, milk, salt, food grain, organic manure, and defense/military equipment by a GTA is entirely exempt from GST.

Q4: If I hire a local tempo for ₹1,000 and he doesn’t issue a consignment note, do I pay RCM? A: No. Since no consignment note is issued, the transporter is not classified as a GTA. The service is exempt from GST, and no RCM liability arises.

CGST, SGST, IGST & UTGST: Key Differences, Rules & Practical Calculation Examples (2026)
Understand the four pillars of Indian GST: CGST, SGST, IGST, and UTGST. Learn intra-state vs inter-state supply rules, place of supply mechanisms, tax revenue sharing, and cross-utilization of ITC.

India's "One Nation, One Tax" reform dismantled a convoluted web of cascading indirect taxes—including Central Excise, Service Tax, State VAT, Entry Tax, and Octroi—subsuming them under the unified Goods and Services Tax (GST) framework in July 2017.

However, because India operates as a federal constitutional democracy, taxing powers are shared equally between the Union Government and the States. To facilitate this dual federal structure, GST was bifurcated into four distinct tax components: **CGST**, **SGST**, **IGST**, and **UTGST**.

In this guide, we break down what each component means, when to levy which tax, how revenue is apportioned, and the strict rules governing Input Tax Credit (ITC) utilization.

---

## Calculate Your Exact GST Split Instantly

Unsure whether your invoice should split into CGST + SGST or single IGST? Run your numbers through our **[Free GST Calculator](/gst-calculator)** to see the exact tax breakdown based on supply type.

---

## Quick Comparison: The 4 GST Types

| Component | Full Form | Governing Act | Levied By | Applied When? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **CGST** | Central Goods and Services Tax | CGST Act, 2017 | Central Government | Intra-State Supply (Within same State) |
| **SGST** | State Goods and Services Tax | Respective State GST Acts | State Government | Intra-State Supply (Within same State) |
| **UTGST** | Union Territory GST | UTGST Act, 2017 | Central / UT Administration | Intra-UT Supply (UT without legislature) |
| **IGST** | Integrated GST | IGST Act, 2017 | Central Government (Shared with Destination State) | Inter-State Supply, Imports & Exports |

---

## 1. Intra-State Supply: CGST + SGST (or UTGST)

An **Intra-State Supply** occurs whenever the **Location of the Supplier** and the **Place of Supply (POS)** are in the **same State or Union Territory**.

### The 50:50 Statutory Split:
Whenever an intra-state supply takes place, the total applicable GST rate is split equally:
- 50% goes to the Central Government as **CGST**.
- 50% goes to the State Government as **SGST** (or **UTGST** if in a Union Territory without legislature).

#### Example:
A consumer in Pune (Maharashtra) buys a television costing ₹50,000 (taxed at 18% GST) from a retail showroom in Mumbai (Maharashtra):
- **Location of Supplier:** Maharashtra
- **Place of Supply:** Maharashtra
- **Tax Classification:** Intra-State Supply
- **CGST (9%):** ₹4,500 (Remitted to Central Treasury)
- **SGST (9%):** ₹4,500 (Remitted to Maharashtra State Treasury)
- **Total Invoice Price:** ₹59,000

---

## 2. Inter-State Supply: IGST (Integrated GST)

An **Inter-State Supply** occurs whenever:
1. The **Location of the Supplier** and the **Place of Supply** are in **different States**.
2. The supplier and place of supply are in **two different Union Territories**, or in a **State and a Union Territory**.
3. **Import of Goods or Services** into India (deemed inter-state under Section 7(2) of IGST Act).
4. **Export of Goods or Services** out of India (deemed inter-state under Section 7(5) of IGST Act).
5. Supplies made to or by a **Special Economic Zone (SEZ)** unit or developer.

### The Single Tax Mechanism:
In an inter-state supply, the taxpayer does not split the tax. A single combined tax called **Integrated GST (IGST)** is charged at the full statutory rate.

#### Example:
A textile mill in Surat (Gujarat) sells cotton yarn worth ₹1,00,000 (taxed at 5%) to a garment manufacturer in Tiruppur (Tamil Nadu):
- **Location of Supplier:** Gujarat
- **Place of Supply:** Tamil Nadu
- **Tax Classification:** Inter-State Supply
- **IGST (5%):** ₹5,00,000 × 5% = **₹5,000**
- **Revenue Sharing:** The central government collects the ₹5,000 IGST and later transfers Tamil Nadu's 50% share (₹2,50) to the destination state under Section 17 of the IGST Act.

---

## 3. What is UTGST & Which Territories Use It?

India has eight Union Territories, but they are not all treated identically under GST law:

### Union Territories WITH Legislature (Treated as "States"):
- **Delhi**, **Puducherry**, and **Jammu & Kashmir** have their own elected legislative assemblies.
- For the purpose of GST, they are legally classified as **States**. Therefore, intra-state transactions within Delhi attract **CGST + SGST** (Delhi GST), not UTGST.

### Union Territories WITHOUT Legislature (Use UTGST):
- **Chandigarh**, **Lakshadweep**, **Daman & Diu and Dadra & Nagar Haveli**, **Andaman & Nicobar Islands**, and **Ladakh**.
- Intra-territory transactions within these regions attract **CGST + UTGST** (Union Territory Goods and Services Tax).

---

## The Rule of Order: ITC Cross-Utilization (Section 49)

Understanding how you can offset input credits against output liabilities is vital for error-free return filing in GSTR-3B:

```
Available ITC Priority Utilization Order:

1. IGST Credit Must be Exhausted First:
   • Offset IGST Output Liability first
   • Any remaining IGST ITC can offset CGST or SGST/UTGST in any proportion

2. CGST Credit:
   • Offset CGST Output Liability first
   • Offset IGST Output Liability second
   • NEVER allowed to offset SGST/UTGST!

3. SGST / UTGST Credit:
   • Offset SGST/UTGST Output Liability first
   • Offset IGST Output Liability second
   • NEVER allowed to offset CGST!
```

> **The Golden Rule:** CGST credit can never cross over to pay SGST, and SGST credit can never pay CGST.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### What happens if I accidentally charge IGST instead of CGST + SGST?
Under **Section 77 of the CGST Act**, if a taxpayer inadvertently pays IGST on a transaction that is subsequently held to be an intra-state supply (CGST+SGST):
- You must deposit the correct CGST + SGST liability.
- You can file an application for **100% refund of the wrongly paid IGST**.
- Crucially, under Section 77(1), **no interest is charged** on the belated payment of CGST/SGST in such bona fide cases.

### Can an unregistered end-consumer claim back SGST?
No. An unregistered retail consumer cannot claim Input Tax Credit; GST forms part of their final out-of-pocket consumption cost.

Complete List of GST Exempted Goods & Services in India: Master 2026 Directory & Rules
Comprehensive guide to 100% GST exempted goods and services in India for 2026. Learn the unbranded food rules, healthcare & educational exemptions, and ITC reversal impact under Rule 42.

While the Indian Goods and Services Tax (GST) applies broadly across commercial activity, the Central Government—exercising powers under **Section 11 of the CGST Act** and **Section 6 of the IGST Act**—statutorily exempts hundreds of essential goods and basic public services from tax in the public interest.

However, dealing in exempt supplies carries severe compliance consequences: **under Section 17(2) read with Rule 42 and Rule 43 of the CGST Rules, businesses making exempt supplies cannot claim Input Tax Credit (ITC)** on related inward purchases and must perform monthly credit reversals.

In this master directory, we compile the complete, updated list of major exempt goods and services for 2026 and analyze the compliance requirements for exempt dealers.

---

## Look Up Any Item's Exemption Status

Unsure whether a product, agricultural item, or service is 0% exempt or taxable? Search our **[GST Rate & HSN/SAC Finder](/gst-rate-finder)** for real-time rates and notifications.

---

## 1. Master List of Major Exempt Goods (Notification 2/2017-CT(R))

Under GST law, goods are exempt primarily to protect food security, agriculture, healthcare, and handloom traditions.

### Agricultural Produce, Live Animals & Fresh Food (Unbranded & Non-Prepackaged):
- **Fresh Fruits and Vegetables:** Fresh potatoes, tomatoes, onions, garlic, apples, bananas, mangoes, etc. (HSN 0701 - 0810).
- **Fresh / Chilled Meat & Fish:** Not frozen or processed, without branding (HSN 0201 - 0302).
- **Fresh Milk, Curd, Lassi, Buttermilk & Paneer:** Sold loose/unlabeled (HSN 0401 - 0406).
- **Fresh Eggs & Natural Honey:** Sold loose without registered brand labels (HSN 0407 - 0409).
- **Cereal Grains (Wheat, Rice, Maize, Barley, Oats):** Unpackaged, unbranded grains sold in loose sacks (HSN 1001 - 1008).
- **Flours (Atta, Maida, Besan, Suji):** Sold loose/unbranded (HSN 1101 - 1106).
- **Live Animals & Birds:** Cattle, sheep, goats, poultry, bees (excluding racehorses) (HSN 0101 - 0106).

> **The Pre-Packaged & Labeled Rule:**  
> Since July 2022, if food staples (pulses, curd, flour, rice) are **pre-packaged and labeled** in quantities up to 25 kg/liters under Legal Metrology Act provisions, they lose their exemption and attract **5% GST**. Loose sales remain 100% exempt.

### Essential Household, Educational & Cultural Items:
- **Salt:** Pure iodized and common salt (HSN 2501).
- **Printed Books, Maps, Newspapers & Periodicals:** Standard printed books and children's drawing books (HSN 4901, 4902, 4905).
- **Bindi, Sindoor, Kumkum, Alta & Bangles:** Plastic/glass bangles (HSN 7117, 9608).
- **Handlooms & Khadi:** Handloom fabrics, khadi yarn sold through KVIC institutions.
- **National Flags & Postal Stamps:** Indian tricolor and postal envelopes issued by India Post.
- **Human Blood, Organs & Semen:** For medical transfusion and clinical storage (HSN 3002).

---

## 2. Master List of Major Exempt Services (Notification 12/2017-CT(R))

### Healthcare & Social Welfare Services:
- **Core Clinical Healthcare:** Diagnosis, medical consultations, surgical treatments by hospitals, doctors, and clinics (Entry 74).
- **Ambulance Services:** Patient emergency transport (Entry 74).
- **Rehabilitation & Mental Wellness:** Services by clinical psychologists and rehabilitation centers.
- **Old Age Homes:** Accommodation and meals provided to residents aged 60+ up to ₹25,000 per month per member.

### Educational Services:
- **Recognized Pre-Schools, Schools & Higher Education:** Education leading to a recognized degree or qualification (Entry 66).
- **Mid-day Meals & School Transportation:** Services provided to educational institutions catering to nursery to Class 12 students.

### Transportation Services:
- **Passenger Rail Transport:** Non-AC railway coaches, suburban local trains, and ordinary metro rail.
- **Non-AC Public Buses:** State road transport non-AC stage carriages.
- **Inland Waterways & Ferries:** Public passenger water transport.
- **Transportation of Agricultural Produce:** Freight transport of milk, salt, foodgrains, and organic fertilizers by rail or road.

### Financial, Real Estate & Government Services:
- **Interest on Loans & Deposits:** Bank interest earned on savings accounts, fixed deposits, and loans (Entry 27).
- **Residential Renting for Living:** Residential dwelling rented to an **unregistered individual** for personal residence (Entry 12).
- **Sovereign Regulatory Functions:** Services by RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, and pure municipal governance functions.

---

## The Compliance Burden: Rule 42 & 43 ITC Reversal

Operating a business that sells both taxable and exempt goods (e.g., a supermarket selling branded shampoo at 18% and loose wheat at 0%) requires rigorous mathematical compliance:

### How Section 17(2) Works:
- Where goods or services are used partly for effecting taxable supplies and partly for exempt supplies, the amount of credit attributable to exempt supplies **must be reversed**.
- **Rule 42 (Inputs & Input Services):** Monthly mathematical apportionment of common ITC (shop rent, electricity, ERP subscriptions) based on the ratio of exempt turnover to total turnover.
- **Rule 43 (Capital Goods):** Reversal of capital goods ITC (refrigerators, billing counters, forklifts) over a statutory 60-month useful life.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### What is the difference between Nil-Rated, Exempt, and Non-GST Supplies?
- **Exempt Supplies:** Goods/services specifically exempted via notification under Section 11 of the CGST Act (e.g., fresh milk, hospital diagnosis).
- **Nil-Rated Supplies:** Items assigned a 0% tax tariff in the GST rate schedule (e.g., grains, salt).
- **Non-GST Supplies:** Commodities constitutionally outside the scope of GST (petroleum, high-speed diesel, aviation turbine fuel, natural gas, crude oil, and alcoholic liquor for human consumption).

### Do I need to issue a Tax Invoice for exempt goods?
No. Under Section 31(3)(c), a registered person supplying exempt goods or services cannot issue a Tax Invoice. Instead, they must issue a **Bill of Supply** showing 0% tax.

The Consequences of Dealing with Fake GST Bills
Claiming ITC on a fake invoice can lead to severe penalties, interest, and even arrest. Learn how to protect your business.

Fake invoicing is a multi-crore problem under the GST regime. Unscrupulous entities generate fake bills to artificially inflate turnover, obtain bank loans, or pass on fraudulent Input Tax Credit (ITC) to buyers. 

As a genuine business owner, you might unknowingly accept a fake bill from a vendor. However, the tax department views the claimant of the ITC (you) as equally responsible. This is why using a [GSTIN Validator](/gstin-validator) is a non-negotiable step in modern accounting.

## What Constitutes a Fake Bill?

A fake invoice under GST typically falls into one of these categories:
1. **Invoice without Goods/Services**: An invoice is issued, but no actual delivery of goods or provision of services takes place.
2. **Fake GSTIN**: The invoice bears a GST number that doesn't exist, has an invalid format, or belongs to someone else.
3. **Cancelled GSTIN**: The supplier's GST registration was cancelled, but they continue to issue tax invoices.

## The Penalties for the Buyer

If you claim ITC on a fake bill, the Directorate General of GST Intelligence (DGGI) can take severe action against your business:

### 1. Reversal of ITC + 18% Interest
The tax department will demand immediate reversal of the wrongly claimed ITC. On top of that, you will be charged **18% interest per annum** under Section 50 of the CGST Act from the date the ITC was wrongly utilized. (You can estimate such penalties using our [Late Fee Calculator](/late-fee-calculator)).

### 2. Equal Penalty (100%)
Under Section 122 of the CGST Act, taking or utilizing ITC without the actual receipt of goods/services attracts a penalty equal to the tax amount evaded or ITC claimed, whichever is higher.

### 3. Prosecution and Arrest

DRC-07 Notice Meaning & 90-Day Action Plan: Recovery Powers, Appeals & Amnesty Relief
Received Form GST DRC-07 Summary of the Order? Understand what DRC-07 legally means, Section 79 recovery powers, the 90-day APL-01 appeal window, and Section 128A waiver relief.

Finding an order in **Form GST DRC-07** uploaded to your GST portal is a critical legal event. Unlike preliminary scrutiny notices (ASMT-10) or show cause notices (DRC-01), **DRC-07 is the formal Summary of the Order** passed by the Proper Officer creating a final, binding pecuniary debt against your business.

Once DRC-07 is uploaded, the clock starts ticking immediately: you have exactly **three months (90 days)** to either pay the adjudicated demand or file a statutory first appeal before the Commissioner (Appeals). If you do neither, the tax department is legally authorized under **Section 79** to initiate aggressive recovery proceedings, including freezing your bank accounts and seizing goods.

In this operational guide, we explain the legal ramifications of DRC-07, the precise 90-day defense roadmap, and how the **Section 128A Amnesty Scheme** can wipe out 100% of interest and penalties.

---

## Check Your Amnesty Eligibility for DRC-07

If your DRC-07 relates to FY 2017-18, FY 2018-19, or FY 2019-20 under Section 73, you may not have to pay full interest or penalties. Check your waiver status on our **[GST Amnesty Tracker](/gst-amnesty-tracker)**.

---

## What is Form GST DRC-07?

Under **Rule 142(5) of the CGST Rules, 2017**, whenever an adjudicating officer concludes assessment or adjudication proceedings under Sections 62, 63, 64, 73, 74, 122, 125, 127, 129, or 130, they must issue a speaking order along with a summary thereof in **Form GST DRC-07**.

### Key Contents of DRC-07:
1. **Reference Number & Date of Order**: Sets the legal limitation clock.
2. **Financial Year & Section**: Indicates whether demand was created under Section 73 (non-fraud) or Section 74 (fraud).
3. **Pecuniary Breakup**: Itemized liability across CGST, SGST, IGST, Cess, Interest under Section 50, and Penalties.
4. **Electronic Liability Ledger Posting**: The demand is automatically debited to your Liability Register Part II (Form GST PMT-01).

---

## The 90-Day Timeline: What Happens If You Do Nothing?

Under **Section 78 of the CGST Act**, any amount payable by a taxable person in pursuance of an order passed under this Act must be paid within a period of **three months (90 days)** from the date of service of the order.

```
Day 0: DRC-07 Issued & Debited to Electronic Liability Ledger
  │
  ├─► Days 1 to 90: Statutory Appeal Window (Form GST APL-01)
  │   Pay 10% Disputed Tax Pre-Deposit ➔ Automatic Stay on Recovery
  │
  └─► Day 91+: Section 79 Recovery Powers Triggered
      • Notice to Bankers (Sec 79(1)(c)) ➔ Bank Account Attachment
      • Notice to Debtors ➔ Garnishee Orders
      • Seizure & Auction of Movable/Immovable Assets
```

---

## The 90-Day Action Plan: 3 Strategic Pathways

### Pathway A: File a Statutory Appeal in Form GST APL-01 (Recommended If Disputed)
If you disagree with the officer's findings on factual or legal grounds:
1. File an appeal before the First Appellate Authority (Commissioner Appeals) under Section 107 within **3 months** (condonable by 1 month if sufficient cause is shown).
2. Pay the **mandatory 10% pre-deposit** of the disputed tax amount via electronic cash ledger.
3. The moment the appeal is acknowledged, the remaining **90% demand is automatically stayed**, barring the recovery officer from freezing your accounts.

### Pathway B: Apply for Section 128A Amnesty Scheme (Full Waiver of Interest & Penalties)
If your DRC-07 order:
- Was issued under **Section 73** (non-fraud), AND
- Pertains to **FY 2017-18, 2018-19, or 2019-20**:
You can avail full relief under Section 128A. By paying **100% of the basic tax amount** on or before the notified date, **100% of the interest and penalties are permanently waived**, and all proceedings are legally deemed concluded.

### Pathway C: File for Installment Facility under Section 80
If the demand is genuine but your business faces temporary liquidity constraints:
- Apply to the Commissioner under **Section 80** requesting permission to pay the demand in monthly installments (up to a maximum of **24 installments**).
- Note: The installment facility is not available for amounts less than ₹25,000 and carries statutory interest under Section 50.

---

## Common Grounds for Challenging DRC-07 Orders

1. **Ex-Parte Order without Personal Hearing:** If the Proper Officer issued DRC-07 without scheduling a personal hearing as mandated by **Section 75(4)**, file a Writ Petition before the High Court or challenge it in appeal for violation of natural justice.
2. **Order Beyond SCN Allegations:** Under **Section 75(7)**, the amount of tax, interest, and penalty demanded in the order cannot exceed the amount specified in the original DRC-01 notice, nor can the officer decide on grounds not raised in the SCN.
3. **Absence of a Reasoned (Speaking) Order:** A DRC-07 that merely states "Taxpayer reply examined and not satisfactory" without assigning detailed judicial reasons is bad in law.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### What is the difference between DRC-07 and DRC-08?
While DRC-07 is the original Summary of Demand passed by the adjudicating officer, **DRC-08 is the Summary of Rectification or Withdrawal Order** issued when an error apparent on the face of the record is corrected under Section 161.

### Can an officer attach my bank account before 90 days?
Under the proviso to Section 78, if the Proper Officer has compelling reasons to believe that the recovery of tax will be frustrated if 3 months are allowed, they may, with the prior approval of the Commissioner, require payment within an expedited period (e.g., 15 days). However, such power cannot be exercised routinely without written recording of emergency reasons.

E-Commerce GST Compliance Checklist & Calendar: Amazon, Flipkart & Meesho Sellers (2026)
Master GST compliance for Amazon, Flipkart, and Meesho sellers. Learn Section 52 TCS credit claiming, GSTR-8 matching, state-wise FBA registration, customer returns, and monthly filing schedules.

Selling products online via marketplaces like Amazon India, Flipkart, Meesho, or Nykaa offers unprecedented reach. However, e-commerce sellers are subject to the strictest indirect tax oversight in India.

Unlike offline brick-and-mortar retailers who file basic monthly returns, online sellers must account for **Tax Collected at Source (TCS) under Section 52**, reconcile marketplace settlement sheets against GSTR-1, claim credit for customer returns across state borders, and obtain multi-state GSTINs for **Fulfilled by Amazon (FBA)** or Flipkart Advantage warehouses.

In this guide, we provide a complete compliance checklist and monthly calendar designed specifically for Indian e-commerce merchants.

---

## E-Commerce GST Compliance Calendar (Monthly Deadlines)

| Date | Statutory Filing / Action | Marketplace Relevance | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **10th of every month** | **Form GSTR-8** filed by E-Commerce Platforms | Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho file GSTR-8 detailing net sales & TCS deducted from you | Data flows to your GST portal |
| **11th of every month** | **Form GSTR-1** (Outward Supplies) | Mandatory deadline for sellers to report state-wise B2C and B2B sales | Late filing blocks GSTR-3B |
| **14th of every month** | **Accept TCS Credit** in GST Portal | Navigate to *Services → Returns → TDS and TCS Received* | Credits flow to your Electronic Cash Ledger |
| **20th of every month** | **Form GSTR-3B** (Payment of Tax) | Discharge net tax liability using available ITC and claimed TCS credits | Strict late fees and interest apply past due date |
| **Quarterly / Annual** | **FBA Warehouse Inventory Reconciliation** | Match physical warehouse stock in other states against ERP stock registers | Avoid stock shortage notices |

## The 5-Point E-Commerce Compliance Checklist

### 1. Section 52 TCS Deduction & Claiming Workflow
Under **Section 52 of the CGST Act**, e-commerce operators deduct **Tax Collected at Source (TCS)** at the rate of **0.5% (0.25% CGST + 0.25% SGST) or 0.5% IGST** on the net value of taxable supplies made through their platform.
- **How to Recover Your Money:** Marketplace TCS does not sit in a vacuum. Once Amazon/Flipkart files Form GSTR-8 on the 10th:
  1. Log in to `gst.gov.in`.
  2. Navigate to **Services** → **Returns** → **TDS and TCS Credit Received**.
  3. Review the auto-drafted net sales and TCS deductions, and click **Accept**.
  4. The accepted TCS amount is **instantly credited to your Electronic Cash Ledger**, which you can use directly to pay your GSTR-3B taxes or claim as a cash refund!

### 2. Fulfilled by Amazon (FBA) & Principal Place of Business (PPoB / APoB)
If you enroll in Amazon FBA or Flipkart Smart Fulfillment to offer Prime 1-day delivery, your inventory is physically stored in marketplace fulfillment centers located in different states (e.g., Haryana, Karnataka, Telangana, Maharashtra).
- **Statutory Rule:** You **cannot** store inventory in another state without obtaining a GST registration in that state.
- **The Process:** You must obtain a separate GSTIN in each state where an FBA warehouse is located, registering Amazon/Flipkart's warehouse as an **Additional Place of Business (APoB)** using their formal consent letter and municipal trade license.

### 3. State-Wise B2C Reporting (Table 7 of GSTR-1)
When selling to end-consumers across India (B2C):
- Every sale must be reported based on the **Place of Supply (POS)**, which is the delivery location of the customer.
- Under **Table 7 of GSTR-1**, you must disclose gross inter-state supplies state-by-state at respective tax rates (e.g., sales to Uttar Pradesh at 18%, sales to Tamil Nadu at 12%).

### 4. Handling High Customer Return Rates (RTO)
High Return-to-Origin (RTO) and customer return rates (often 20% to 35% in fashion and footwear) create significant accounting headaches:
- When a customer returns an item, the marketplace issues a negative credit adjustment in their settlement report.
- **GST Reconciliation:** In your GSTR-1, outward sales must be reported **net of sales returns / credit notes**. If your credit notes in a particular state exceed fresh sales in a given month, the net negative figure can be carried forward to subsequent months.

### 5. Reconciling Marketplace Inward Fee Invoices
Amazon and Flipkart issue monthly B2B tax invoices to you for:
- Marketplace Referral Fees & Closing Fees
- FBA Pick & Pack Fees and Storage Fees
- In-platform Advertising / Sponsored Product Ads
- Logistics & Shipping Charges  
Ensure these inward invoices appear in your **GSTR-2B** so your business claims the full **18% Input Tax Credit** on these platform expenses.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### Can small e-commerce sellers with turnover below ₹40 Lakhs sell without GST?
Under recent GST Council relaxations, intra-state sellers with turnover below the threshold (₹40L for goods) can sell goods through e-commerce operators without mandatory GST registration, provided they obtain an **Enrolment Number** on the GST portal. However, these unregistered sellers **cannot make inter-state supplies** and cannot store goods in out-of-state FBA warehouses.

### What should I do if Amazon's GSTR-8 figures do not match my sales register?
If there is a variance between Amazon's reported GSTR-8 sales and your internal sales reports (often due to transit timing differences at month-end), accept the undisputed records on the portal and claim the variance in the subsequent month's reconciliation.

E-Way Bill Validity Period: How Distance Decides Your Deadline
Don't let your e-way bill expire in transit. Learn the exact e-way bill validity period rules for 2026, how distance dictates time limits, and extension rules.

Generating an E-Way Bill is only half the battle. Once you hit submit on the portal and generate that 12-digit number, a ticking clock begins. If a tax inspector intercepts your delivery vehicle and finds that the e way bill validity period has expired, it is treated legally as if you are moving goods without an e-way bill at all. The result? Immediate seizure of goods and a penalty of 200% of the tax amount. To prevent this logistical nightmare, every supplier and transporter must understand exactly how to calculate e way bill validity based on the distance the truck needs to travel.
Quick Answer: For standard vehicles, an e-way bill is valid for 1 day for the first 200 kilometers, plus 1 additional day for every subsequent 200 km (or part thereof). For Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC), it is valid for 1 day for the first 20 km, plus 1 additional day for every subsequent 20 km.
## The 200 km Rule: How to Calculate E Way Bill Validity When the GST system was first introduced, the rule was 1 day for every 100 km. However, to push for faster logistics and prevent the misuse of documents, the government tightened the eway bill time limit. Currently, the validity is strictly tied to a **200 km per day** baseline for regular conveyances (standard trucks, tempos, and trains). ### Example Scenarios: **Scenario 1: Short Distance Delivery** You are transporting goods from a warehouse in Delhi to a retailer in Noida. The distance is 45 km. - **Validity:** Since 45 km is under the 200 km threshold, the e-way bill is valid for **1 day**. **Scenario 2: Medium Distance Delivery** You are shipping goods from Mumbai to Surat. The distance entered on the portal is 285 km. - **Validity:** The first 200 km grants 1 day. The remaining 85 km (which is a "part thereof" of the next 200 km block) grants 1 additional day. Total validity = **2 days**. **Scenario 3: Long Haul Delivery** You are moving inventory from Chennai to Hyderabad. The distance is 630 km. - 0 to 200 km = 1 day - 201 to 400 km = 1 day - 401 to 600 km = 1 day - 601 to 630 km = 1 day - **Total Validity:** **4 days**. 👉 Try it yourself: Stop doing mental math. Use our **[E-Way Bill Validity Calculator](/eway-bill-validity)** to instantly determine exactly how many days your shipment has before it expires. Need to calculate the motorable road distance between your dispatch and delivery postal codes? Use our free **[Pin to Pin Distance Calculator](/pin-to-pin-distance-calculator)** and read the **[Pin to Pin Distance Rules Guide](/blog/pin-to-pin-distance-calculation-eway-bill-rules)**. ## Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC) Exception If you are transporting heavy machinery, wind turbine blades, or large infrastructure equipment, your truck simply cannot travel 200 km in a single day. The government accounts for this with a specific Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC) exception. For ODC shipments, the validity is calculated at a severely reduced rate: - **1 day for the first 20 km** - **1 additional day for every subsequent 20 km (or part thereof)** If you are moving an ODC shipment 285 km, your validity period will be 15 days, not 2 days. ## When Exactly Does "1 Day" End? A common mistake is assuming that "1 day" means 24 hours from the exact minute you generated the bill. This is incorrect. In the e-way bill system, validity periods expire at **midnight (11:59:59 PM)**. **Crucial Example:** If you generate a 1-day e-way bill on Tuesday at 4:00 PM, that bill is valid until midnight of the *following* day (Wednesday at 11:59:59 PM). You essentially get the remainder of Tuesday, plus all of Wednesday.
